protocolitos.text:
Lupita and Frida combine fresh medicinal herbs for traditional Aztec remedies that Lupita can sell to tourists. They agree to share their resources, helping each other weather economic storms. Both commit to attending weekly community meetings to discuss mutual aid efforts and address social tensions.

The protocolitos are:
- Lupita supplies Frida with fruits and vegetables.
- Frida gives Lupita traditional Aztec remedies.
- Regularly attend community meetings for mutual support.
protocolitos.narrative:
Status: uncertain
Title: Lupita and Frida's Mutual Aid Protocol
Summary: The protocolito aims to have Lupita and Frida help each other by sharing resources and attending community meetings. However, given the limited infrastructure and scarce tools available, it remains unclear if this mutual aid effort will be successful.
Capacity: Both Lupita and Frida are overcommitted with their existing roles as street vendors and community organizers. They struggle to find time for this new shared venture.
Conflict: The lack of resources and minimal shared infrastructure creates a bottleneck that may impede the success of their agreement to combine fruits, vegetables, and remedies.
Implementation: Despite their best intentions, Lupita and Frida were unable to fully execute this protocolito due to limited capacity and competing priorities. They made some progress in sharing resources but fell short of attending weekly meetings.
Effects:
- Some exchange of fruits, vegetables, and remedies occurred between them
- Their time constraints prevented consistent coordination and support through community meetings
Production: Exchange of traditional Aztec remedies between Lupita and Frida.
Quantity: A limited number of remedy batches were shared each week based on their harvests and production capacity. 
Quality: The quality of the remedies was high due to Frida's expertise, but the quantity was constrained by their resource limitations and competing commitments.

To move forward, they will need to find ways to better align their existing commitments with the goals of the mutual aid protocolito, while also building out basic infrastructures like transport and communication channels.
